# Node level 6 and 9 matching in zlib-rs 0.6.7

Source: the published [zlib-rs 0.6.7 crate](https://crates.io/crates/zlib-rs/0.6.7), registry checksum `34b31d188d9d685a4f9c7b46d6e36631b07058d2cfe190267adce54dc230bf12`. The upstream Zlib license and source files are preserved. This is an altered source distribution, not an unmodified upstream release.

The opt-in `scriptc-node-level6` feature changes the algorithm function for compression level 6 in `src/deflate/algorithm/mod.rs`, from `deflate_medium` to the existing `deflate_slow`. In `src/deflate/algorithm/slow.rs`, level 6 also admits insertion when three bytes of lookahead remain, instead of requiring four; the fourth hash byte comes from the initialized padding maintained by `fill_window`. In `src/deflate/hash_calc.rs`, level 6 uses Node's default-memLevel four-byte hash, `((value + 1) * 66521 >> 16) & 32767`, with wrapping 32-bit arithmetic, for single and batched insertions. That computation was independently checked in the installed Node 26.10.0 and Node 24.15.0 executables; it is not inferred from the unrelated Chromium CRC32C implementation.

In `src/deflate/algorithm/slow.rs`, the same opt-in level-6 path also rejects three-byte matches at distances greater than 4096 bytes, matching Node's `TOO_FAR` heuristic even with the default strategy. The existing filtered-strategy rejection remains unchanged. This is an algorithm rule for any input, not a special case for a package, file format or fixture.

The numeric level, good-match threshold 8, lazy-match threshold 16, nice-match length 128, chain limit 128, window, memory level, framing, decompression and all other compression levels except 9 remain unchanged. The runtime admits only the default memory/window configuration for this projection; this patch does not qualify custom memory levels. This feature is enabled by the scriptc runtime; without it, upstream behavior is retained. The feature is declared in both Cargo manifests. All changed algorithm code is safe Rust; the runtime's `forbid(unsafe_code)` remains in place, and no C compressor is introduced.

Node's [pinned 24.15.0 deflate source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nodejs/node/v24.15.0/deps/zlib/deflate.c) uses slow matching for level 6 with those parameters. Local Node 26.10.0 and Node 24.15.0 produce the same bytes for the differential vectors used here. Node 26's project pin remains 26.8.1; local 26.10.0 evidence does not substitute for running that pin.

The original mismatch is reproducible with `"abc".repeat(89)`: Node emits raw hex `4b4c4a4e1c45600400`, while unmodified zlib-rs emits `4b4c4a4e1c4549a0400000`. Choosing slow at the original level-6 tuning removes this partitioning difference without pretending level 6 is level 7. A separate minimized input `02000302000302` exposes the terminal three-byte match: Node emits `63626066022200`, while slow with the upstream insertion threshold still emits `636260666260660200`. Input `82f90493d6f9049356` distinguishes the hash choice even after fixing the insertion threshold: Node emits `6bfac932f91a10870100`, while the upstream hash produces `6bfac932f9da4f96c96100`. Compiler regression coverage lives in `packages/compiler/test/zlib-node-parity.test.ts` and `tests/corpus/3411` to `3414`; runtime tests cover framing, level identity and both minimized inputs.

Corpus program `tests/corpus/3443-zlib-distant-three-byte-match.ts` and the corresponding runtime test pin distances 4095, 4096, 4097 and 8192, including a three-byte match whose following byte differs. Before the distance heuristic was restored, the latter two inputs differed from both local Nodes; dev and release Rust binaries now match their stdout, stderr and exit status. A separate local consumer check rebuilt the unchanged redwall PNG codec and compared complete encoded files for all six original 3840×2160 wallpapers against Node 26.10.0 and Node 24.15.0; all six files and process outputs match. This qualifies that codec scenario, not the full redwall application.

The same feature also covers level 9, selected through one predicate, `node_slow_level` in `src/deflate.rs`, so that levels 6 and 9 cannot drift apart. Level 9 already ran `deflate_slow` upstream; the patch makes it follow the same Node rules as level 6 and keeps its own tuning (good-match 32, lazy-match 258, nice-match 258, chain limit 4096). Level 9 uses the four-byte Node hash instead of upstream's rolling three-byte hash (`lm_set_level` selects the standard variant and `fill_window` initializes the hash from the selected variant instead of from the chain limit), it walks chains with the plain `longest_match` instead of upstream's `longest_match_slow` chain jumper, it inserts the terminal three-byte string, and it rejects three-byte matches farther than 4096 bytes. Removing any one of these four rules changes the output of some input: a repeated three-byte tail, `6c206669206669`, `6e207472656520747265662074726565` and the distance 4097 and 8192 vectors each isolate one of them, and the runtime tests carry Node's literal bytes for all of them.

A fifth rule, in `fill_window` in `src/deflate.rs`, applies to levels 6 and 9: the first window slide copies only the `wsize - more` bytes that hold data, as zlib does, instead of the whole upper half. The bytes left behind past the end of the data are read by the final `longest_match` tie-break, so a stream that ends inside the first slide (inputs of about 65274 to 65535 bytes, about 5 percent of compressible inputs of that size) differed from Node in its last few bytes at the default level, at level 9, and in raw and gzip framing until this rule was added. Later slides need no rule: sweeps over the end-of-stream ranges of the second to fourth slide (inputs of 98042 to 98304, 130810 to 131072 and 163578 to 163840 bytes) were identical to Node with and without it, and the fifth (196346 to 196608 bytes) is identical with it. The runtime test `levels_six_and_nine_match_node_when_the_first_window_slide_ends_the_stream` and corpus program `tests/corpus/3487-zlib-first-window-slide-bytes.ts` carry Node's literal lengths and CRC-32 values for inputs inside the range and on both sides of it.

The 2026-10-05 measurement compared the vendored compressor, driven through the runtime's 16 KiB output-chunk loop, with the Node 26.8.1 and Node 24.15.0 executables on one x86-64 Linux host, each Node run separately. Level 9 output was identical on 483 deterministic inputs (empty, one byte, short and long text, random bytes, periodic data, run-length data, small alphabets, planted far matches, already-compressed data, synthetic PNG scanlines and a real 33179760 byte 3840x2160 scanline raster, which is what the Redwall renderer compresses with `{ level: 9 }`) and on 7,150 pseudo-random inputs of 0 to 3,000,000 bytes. Levels 6 and 0 were identical on the same 483 inputs and on 5,150 and 5,950 of the pseudo-random ones. Node 26.8.1 and Node 24.15.0 agreed with each other on every deterministic input, and each agreed with the compressor. This is a finite sample on one host, not a proof for arbitrary inputs; other CPUs and operating systems were not measured. A second pass swept every size from 65200 to 65700, from 98000 to 98400, from 130700 to 131200, from 163500 to 163900, from 196300 to 196700, from 32600 to 32900 and from 262100 to 262300 over six content families (four-letter text, copy-heavy data, random bytes, words, runs and image-like rows) at levels 9, 6 and 0 against both Node executables: 0 differences in 48,726 comparisons per Node after the first-slide rule, where the same sweep of 65200 to 65700 at level 9 had differed on 35 of 3006 inputs before it.

Level 0 needs no zlib-rs change. Stored blocks are cut against the output space the caller offers, so the runtime's one-shot loop (`packages/runtime-rust/src/zlib.rs`) hands the compressor 16 KiB at a time like Node does, and the stored block layout (65531, then 32773, then 32768-byte blocks) matches Node. The 32 KiB growth strategy used before produced 65535-byte blocks for inputs above 64 KiB.

This patch does not claim universal bit-identical compression, including levels 6 and 9, nor parity for levels 1 to 5, 7 and 8, which have independently observed differences or were not measured. A deterministic extra prototype probe of 160 byte inputs had zero level-6 differences against both local Nodes after the original three changes; that finite sample is not a compatibility percentage or proof for arbitrary inputs. Any additional behavior must receive its own differential evidence before extending this feature.
